text:
The suspect is not guilty if the jury accepts his account, because a punch used only to stop an unprovoked nightstick beating is reasonable self-defense against excessive force, which this arrest statute leaves in place. He is guilty if the jury accepts the officer’s account, because he then struck first to resist a known arrest. The statute makes submission the duty once an arrest is known, so the assault verdict turns on which account the jury believes.

CONFIDENCE: 86
